prompt: I would like to outperform the S&P 500 in the next year. Can you propose 10 stocks I should buy?
reply:
# 10 Stocks That Could Beat the S&P 500 Over the Next Year

No one can reliably pick stocks that will beat the S&P 500 over a single year. In most years, most professional large-cap fund managers fail to beat it, and over 10+ years roughly 85–90% fall behind (per S&P's SPIVA reports). Also, my knowledge runs to about May 2026 and I don't have live market data, so please check current prices, valuations and news before buying anything.

## The list

This portfolio is a deliberate bet that spending on AI infrastructure keeps growing, balanced with a few names that don't depend on it.

| # | Company (Ticker) | Why it could outperform | Main risk |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM)** | Makes nearly all of the most advanced AI chips; not in the S&P 500, so it adds real differentiation | Taiwan–China conflict |
| 2 | **Broadcom (AVGO)** | Custom AI chips for hyperscalers plus AI networking; recurring VMware software revenue | Depends on a few large customers; expensive valuation |
| 3 | **Alphabet (GOOGL)** | Growth in Google Cloud, its own AI chips (TPUs), Gemini, YouTube and Waymo; often cheaper than big-tech peers | AI chatbots could erode Search; antitrust remedies |
| 4 | **Amazon (AMZN)** | AWS demand from AI, a high-margin ad business, improving retail profits | Heavy spending on data centers could squeeze cash flow |
| 5 | **Microsoft (MSFT)** | Azure and enterprise AI sales (Copilot) | High capital spending; uncertainty around its OpenAI relationship |
| 6 | **Constellation Energy (CEG)** | Largest US nuclear operator; data centers want steady, carbon-free power | Power prices, regulation, rich valuation |
| 7 | **GE Vernova (GEV)** | Large order backlogs for gas turbines and grid equipment as electricity demand rises | Much of this may already be priced in; weak wind business |
| 8 | **Eli Lilly (LLY)** | Leader in obesity and diabetes drugs, with oral versions in development | Drug-pricing pressure, competition, premium valuation |
| 9 | **JPMorgan Chase (JPM)** | Best-run large US bank; gains when deal-making and trading are strong | A credit downturn or recession |
| 10 | **MercadoLibre (MELI)** | Leader in Latin American e-commerce and fintech; not in the S&P 500 | Currency swings, Brazil/Argentina economies, loan losses |

**If you want less AI concentration**, you could swap Microsoft for **Visa (V)** and Constellation for **Costco (COST)** or **Berkshire Hathaway (BRK.B)**. That makes the portfolio steadier but lowers its upside.

## How to improve your odds

1. **Owning index heavyweights barely changes your results.** MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN and AVGO already make up a large share of the S&P 500. Your results will differ from the index mainly through the names outside it (TSM, MELI) and through equal-weighting all ten.
2. **Consider a core-satellite approach.** Keep 70–80% in an S&P 500 index fund and put 20–30% into these picks. You can still beat the index without risking a big shortfall.
3. **Size positions sensibly.** Equal weight (10% each) is a reasonable default. Avoid letting any single stock grow above about 15–20% of your portfolio.
4. **Account for taxes and fees.** Gains on stocks held less than a year are usually taxed at a higher rate, which can erase a small lead over the index. Using a tax-advantaged account helps.
5. **Measure honestly.** Compare your total return, including dividends, against an S&P 500 fund such as VOO or SPY over the same period.
6. **Write down why you bought each stock.** If that reason breaks (for example, AI spending stalls), sell. Don't sell just because the price dipped.

This is general information, not personalized financial advice. If you tell me your time horizon, risk tolerance, how much of your savings this represents, and your country, I can tailor the list.
